classification.difficultyReason: Model two end-of-year contribution streams as geometric series and compare their future values over different durations.

content.prompt:
Asam cannot decide whether to invest $\$1000$ at the end of each year for 15 years or $\$500$ for 30 years in a superannuation fund.

If the interest rate is 5% p.a., which would be the better investment for Asam? Compare the balances at the end of their respective investment periods. Give monetary answers to the nearest cent.

answer.short: Investing $\$500$ annually for 30 years gives $\$33\,219.42$, compared with $\$21\,578.56$ for $\$1000$ annually for 15 years: $\$11\,640.86$ more at the respective investment endpoints.
answer.worked:
Option 1: $\$1000$ at the end of each year for 15 years.

At the end of year 15, the balance is
$$1000(1.05)^{14}+1000(1.05)^{13}+\cdots+1000.$$
This is a geometric series with $a=1000$, common ratio $R=1.05$ and $n=15$.
$$\begin{aligned}FV_1&=\frac{1000(1.05^{15}-1)}{1.05-1}\\FV_1&\approx\$21\,578.56.\end{aligned}$$
Option 2: $\$500$ at the end of each year for 30 years.

At the end of year 30, the balance is
$$500(1.05)^{29}+500(1.05)^{28}+\cdots+500.$$
This is a geometric series with $a=500$, common ratio $R=1.05$ and $n=30$.
$$\begin{aligned}FV_2&=\frac{500(1.05^{30}-1)}{1.05-1}\\FV_2&\approx\$33\,219.42.\end{aligned}$$
Using the unrounded balances,
$$\begin{aligned}FV_2-FV_1&=\frac{500(1.05^{30}-1)-1000(1.05^{15}-1)}{0.05}\\FV_2-FV_1&\approx\$11\,640.86.\end{aligned}$$
Therefore, investing $\$500$ annually for 30 years gives the larger balance at its investment endpoint, by $\$11\,640.86$.
